code.why: Answered only in a World started read-only, whose kernel refuses a command that writes (redis.ReadOnlyError); the life and the published examples walk a World that writes.
The dialect's exec, which the kernel's Redis core calls only for a command in the dialect's own `commands`; Upstash's dialect declares none, so only a defect of the core would reach it.

The descriptor's credentialDoor: the World's runtime calls it at boot to issue an application's Upstash credentials. The life and the published examples make their database and QStash on the console's pages and boot no application; the client cases (twin-world packages/twin-standard/src/clients/upstash.ts) are the application that holds them.
The users door's refusal of a sign-up with no email or password: the World's own door, called by the World with a whole sign-up; no customer of Upstash reaches it.
The destinations door's refusal of a stand-in with no URL or status: the World's own door, which the World calls whole; no customer of Upstash reaches it.
The listening HTTP server wraps the fetch in a runtime host process. In-memory journey walks call fetch directly; they open no listening server.

Rethrows an exception of the kernel's Redis core other than a read-only World's ReadOnlyError (answered beside it, as readOnlyWorld): every command the REST API runs has passed the core's queue-time check, and the core answers a command's own failure as a reply, so only a defect of the core throws here.
The console offers only open, reset and roll actions. This fallback requires posting an action no form offers to the workspace page.
